Good catch! Here’s the revised version:

We had a wonderful stay at Paradisus Palma Real. Everyone we encountered was friendly, welcoming, and eager to help. Our room was cleaned and restocked daily, which made our stay comfortable and stress-free.

The family side of the resort was perfect for us, especially with the Junior Swim-Up Suite. Having easy access to the pool was incredibly convenient and made traveling with a toddler so much easier.

The buffet offered a good variety of food and was best when we went earlier in the day. The specialty restaurants were excellent and were some of our favorite dining experiences during the trip. The concierge service was also extremely helpful, making restaurant reservations simple and ensuring everything went smoothly throughout our stay.

Overall, we had a fantastic vacation and would happily return. We highly recommend Paradisus Palma Real for families looking for a beautiful, relaxing, and family-friendly resort experience.

reviews.text: First time at the Paradisus Palma Real and had a very nice stay. Our stay at Paradisus Palma Real Punta Cana exceeded our expectations and became one of our favorite vacations. We stayed in The Reserve section and from arrival, everything felt effortless.

A special thank you to José, our bellman, who was exceptional from arrival to departure and always made us feel welcome. Our concierge, Christopher Rivera (Chris), truly made this vacation unforgettable. He arranged all of our dinner reservations, constantly checked on us, and made sure we had everything we needed. For my birthday, he helped my husband organize a private beach dinner with a special song playing—it honestly felt like a dream.

Special recognition also goes to Arismendi for making my birthday dinner extra special, Dilania at the pool area for always checking on us, Rafael at the beach for constantly going above and beyond, Carlos for my birthday drink, and Gladys for an incredible massage. Every employee made us feel like family.

Our beachfront walkout room was beautiful and fully stocked with everything we needed. The resort itself is luxurious, spacious, spotless, with plenty of beach chairs, pools, and a beautiful beach.

Brutally honest: we travel often and are hard to impress with food, but the buffet had great variety and authentic Dominican breakfast. Kanna, Asian, the steakhouse, and Italian restaurant were our favorites. Drinks were typical all-inclusive drinks. Nightlife is limited after 11 PM, but if relaxation is what you want, this place delivers.

We travelled as couple, and this hotel is truly amazing. I can highly recommend it. We especially loved the beautiful beach, which, fortunately, is regularly cleared of seaweed by the hotel. The rooms are very spacious and exceptionally clean. There is also a great variety of pools, including an adults-only area. What impressed us the most was the food. We travel very frequently and have rarely experienced such a wide selection of restaurants offering excellent cuisine and extensive menus. There were also plenty of delicious options for vegetarians.
Furthermore, the staff is truly outstanding. We received a very warm welcome, and everyone took excellent care of us throughout our stay. Every request was handled quickly, professionally, and with genuine kindness. During our stay, I proposed to my girlfriend at the beautiful Kanna Beach at the hotel. To arrange everything, I contacted the hotel by email a few weeks in advance and explained my plans. My heartfelt thanks go to Jose R. and Leandro C. I initially planned everything with Jose via email — he took great care of every detail and made my wishes come true. Together with Leandro and an external company, they organized the decorations beautifully. It truly became the proposal of my dreams. Jose and Leandro also took exceptional care of us during our stay, especially considering the amount of coordination the proposal required.  Overall, our stay was absolutely wonderful, and we will definitely return!

I stayed in the Reserve section for two nights. Although the amount I was ultimately charged did not match the amount I was told at check-in, I still think the upgrade was worth it. Since it was my first visit and I do not speak Spanish, having conceirge available to guide me through daily activities and programs was very helpful. Most staff members were kind and helpful. The adult-only pool was clean, relaxing, and not crowded. I also visited the family pool, which was larger and also looked very nice. As a solo traveler, I especially appreciated the calmer atmosphere.
The food was good and there were plenty of options. As a vegetarian with mushroom and eggplant allergies, I still had enough variety. I enjoyed breakfast and lunch at Santé and dinner at Blue Agave. Blue Agave had a lovely atmosphere, but the service there was disappointing. My plates were cleared twice while I was still eating, simply because I was typing on my phone. I asked about dessert options and was told churros & vanilla ice cream fritters. I asked for vanilla ice cream with churros, and after about 5 min I was told they only had chocolate ice cream. I had been there only around 40 minutes, the restaurant was nearly empty, and I felt rushed and unwelcome when I had hoped to enjoy my last evening.
My reservation included spa credit, but I was booked at Zel, so I couldnt use it. My personal concierge was great and arranged a jacuzzi bath both nights. I also enjoyed yoga, zumba, and bachata on the beach.

Very disappointing experience at Paradisus Palma Real Golf & Spa Resort. For the amount of money paid, I expected luxury hospitality and professional management, but unfortunately my entire stay was stressful and unpleasant.

From the first night, management handled situations very poorly and staff were rude, dismissive, and unwelcoming throughout most of the trip. Security treated us in an extremely disrespectful way, and management did nothing meaningful to resolve the situation or make up for the experience.

Housekeeping also failed to clean our room on the first night even after we specifically requested it, which added to the frustration and is one of the reasons I rated cleanliness poorly.

The overall atmosphere of the hotel felt cold and uncomfortable rather than relaxing or luxurious. Aside from one helpful employee named Freddy, customer service across the resort was honestly terrible. Even when issues were brought to management’s attention multiple times, there was no real effort to improve our stay or compensate us for the problems we experienced.

This was supposed to be a relaxing vacation, but it ended up being one of the worst travel experiences I’ve had.

reviews.text:
Overall this resort was a pretty big disappointment.  The main area of the resort (lobby, courtyard, restaurant area) was very nice, scenic, clean and plenty of space to sit around and relax and enjoy the views.  There are plenty of bars with decent drinks and friendly bar tenders.  The staff was very nice and helpful.

The room however was very underwhelming and a pretty big disappointment.  We had the Junior Suite with the Ocean view.  The room had definitely seen better days.  Poorly patched holes and cracks in the walls, a very uncomfortable and stained couch, stains on the walls and furniture, and a pretty persistent mildew smell.  It just seemed run down and their solution was to paint over everything (they even painted over a stray hair on the furniture).  

Finding a spot at the beach was somewhat of a hassle if you didn’t get down early.  People would throw a towel down to claim a spot and not come back for hours, staff didn’t seem to enforce any of the 30 minute rules for leaving a space unattended.  Most of the beachfront is behind expensive cabanas that seemed to go entirely unrented, blocking the view and leading to the beach vendors using them to hang out and lounge on when they weren’t harassing people trying to relax on the beach.  

The food was by far the worst we’ve experienced.   Eating at the buffet was mostly just trying to find things that didn’t look like they would get you sick (we still got sick).  The actual restaurants were a little better.

reviews.text:
Pros:
The property is well maintained and the room is clean. It’s a stunningly beautiful property. The food is very fresh and clearly prepared with care.
Cons:
The hotel management is not good, and it really affected our experience.
1.	We did not receive airport pickup despite filling out their pre-arrival form. When we arrived, our kids had to sleep without pillows the first night because the sofa bed was not made, even though we had requested this in advance.
2.	We had issues at check-in because our room was not available due to a “leak.” We were downgraded to a lesser room for the first night. A “concierge” promised us free spa treatment and water park bracelets as compensation, but it turned out he was actually a sales person trying to get us to buy into their vacation plan (Melia Circle). There were no free spa treatments initially. We had to argue with the front desk for four days in a row just to get them to honor what was promised. It was exhausting and frustrating. Every time we asked to speak to a manager, we had to explain everything again to a new person. I eventually had to call Expedia to file a complaint, and even they could not get in touch with the hotel to resolve the issue.
3.	Do not believe the “free credits” like the $200 resort credit, $50 wine credit, or $100 spa credit listed on your reservation. They look like perks for Expedia guests, but the front desk either doesn’t know about them or refuses to honor them. These are actually tied to their timeshar

We had a wonderful time at Paradisus Hotel.  Upon arrival we were welcomed by our concierge, Alam who was excellent.  He took great care of us, helping to reserve restaurants and checking in to ensure our stay was pleasant.  At the end of our stay Alam made sure our bags were picked up from our room and he was waiting at the lobby to bid us farewell which was a nice touch.  The resort itself is beautiful with plenty of pools and beach front.  The rooms were clean, spacious and very comfortable.  We stayed in the Reserve area which offered some extra perks.  We also got a couples massage which was wonderful.  There was nightly entertainment which was excellent (much better than many other resorts we have stayed at)  There were lots of food options from buffets to à la carte, snack and coffee bars and lots of ice cream - the food was decent. 

Some constructive feedback-  the service at the buffet and restaurants was not great - simple things like filling our water or bringing us coffee seemed like an ongoing challenge but Eventually we did get what we had asked for.  
Also on the first few days, it was challenging to get any beach towels. This was due primarily to some guests taking 3-4 towels each which seems rather excessive.  While I don’t blame the hotel for guest behaviour, I do think they could implement a better system to avoid this.  
Overall our stay was great and we would consider staying at this resort again in the future.

Despite my room being ready, I waited nearly an hour in the Reserve lobby while the front desk agent assisted multiple other guests. The check in experience set the tone for what was to come. 
The Kanna / private members-only area is visually appealing, but unfortunately it highlights how underwhelming the rest of the property is by comparison. I paid $575 to upgrade to The Reserve, and upon arrival, seriously considered leaving altogether.
My first experience with a Reserve-only restaurant was shockingly bad. The host appeared visibly annoyed by my presence, and after being seated, no one approached me for an extended period of time. The food was genuinely inedible. I initially tried the buffet, couldn’t stomach anything, and then ordered from the menu hoping for improvement. It wasn’t. The salad was soggy and unappetizing, and the gazpacho was equally unpleasant.
The two Reserve-only pools were extremely secluded and had no bar service, which made the upgrade feel pointless. Ironically, the large adults-only pool with a swim-up bar was accessible without any Reserve upgrade and was far superior.

reviews.text:
We had a great time, but it wasn’t without some issues. 

We were there for a girl’s trip and had requested a room with two beds. We were given one king bed and they said they didn’t have a room with two beds to accommodate us although it didn’t seem like the resort was at full capacity. The front desk said they would send an extra bed which they did not. After we gave up on that, it took four phone calls and a walk to the front desk to get bedding for the pull out sofa. Also, the app never worked for us with our reservation information. Lastly, as an Expedia booking, we were supposed to get a bottle of wine and welcome amenities which we didn’t receive. The service is very hit or miss here. The entertainment is also minimal and we had no idea what the schedule was since the app didn’t work. There was also no waiter service around the pool or beach. 

As for the great stuff, the resort and the beach are well kept and clean. The beach and the chair selection was great. The food at the buffet was very good as were the Mexican and Steakhouse restaurants. We didn’t have an issue with reservations, but the day we arrived they were full. After that, as long as you book a day in advance there were options. 

Overall, the food and beach are great and if you are looking for a relaxed atmosphere and are good on your own to figure everything out, this place is great. If you are looking for great service, this may not be the place for you.

I booked this trip with my daughter for a quick getaway and booked a junior swim up suite for 4 nights through Expedia. Words cannot describe how frustrated I am with our experience. We took the first flight out of our hometown airport hoping to spend the entire first afternoon in the sun. That did not happen because our room was supposed to be ready no later than 3pm the day of check in. We got the run around after I refused to take two twin beds that we were being offered by the front desk so I feel like I was “black listed” by the front desk team as a result. It took hours to get our room despite having a butler (whom was not able to effectively execute on any request I had for her). It wasn’t until a concierge manager noticed us waiting in the lobby and commented how long we were waiting did we get our room. He took matters into his own hands and personally walked us to our room and I was so grateful. He apologized for the room check in issues but I got no real explanation as to what happened. As an Expedia member I was told early check in would be an option- again didn’t happen for us.

My room wasn’t cleaned for two days and I was told it was as because I didn’t ask for it to be cleaned by pushing the button near the front door. Had my check in experience been handled properly I would have known this button needed to be switched on.

I normally don’t leave negative reviews, but this resort was extremely disappointing. Don’t expect a warm or welcoming atmosphere. Dinner reservations were nearly impossible to get, and we ended up at the buffet most nights—which unfortunately had an unpleasant smell and very limited options.

Lunch spots didn’t require reservations, but the moment you walked in, it often felt like guests were not welcome. Many of the staff members were rude, unprofessional, and communication was very difficult because very few spoke English.

Although the resort advertises itself as family-friendly, the children’s food options were basically limited to chicken nuggets, French fries, and mac and cheese—no vegetables, berries, or healthier choices. The breakfast buffet offered food that was poorly prepared and often difficult to eat. I also noticed concerning hygiene practices; some cooks handled food without gloves and used their hands directly.

Relaxing on the beach was nearly impossible due to constant interruptions every few minutes from people selling souvenirs, tours, and other things. It was overwhelming and made it hard to enjoy the experience.

To make matters worse, several members of our group ended up with a stomach virus during the stay.

Overall, I would not recommend this resort. Avoid if you’re looking for a relaxing, family-friendly vacation with good service and food quality.

I rarely write negative reviews, but our experience at Paradisus Palma Real was alarming. During our stay around Storm Melissa, my wife bit into a piece of glass inside a sushi roll. We caught it in time, but this is a severe food-safety breach with potentially life-threatening consequences.
We also observed flies on exposed items at the buffet on multiple visits—covered stations and active monitoring were clearly lacking.
Finally, during the intense rains from the storm, no porters assisted with transportation around the property. There was no facilitation to reach our room, leaving us to trek through heavy rain with small children—completely avoidable at a resort of this category.
Safety and basic service should come first. The hotel offered a one-night compensation conditional on signing a legal release of liability, which we declined—not the kind of paperwork anyone expects on a family vacation. I sincerely hope management immediately strengthens kitchen QA (including controls to prevent foreign objects and better pest management) and ensures proactive, weather-contingent guest transport during storms. Until then, I cannot recommend this property.

As a frequent traveler and long-time admirer of the Meliá brand, I must say my recent stay did not meet expectations, especially after upgrading to The Reserve, which I believed would offer a superior experience. Our luggage took nearly three hours to reach the room, which upon arrival was not properly cleaned: there was paper left in the bathroom, no slippers, and missing towels. When we asked for replacements, we were told the hotel was full, which is unacceptable for a premium service. Thankfully, Kelvin, our concierge, personally ensured we received the missing items and provided exceptional support throughout our stay.

The promised amenities (a bottle of wine and cookies) arrived late, and overall communication from some staff lacked the warmth and professionalism I associate with Meliá. Yoga sessions were limited, and the Friday class was canceled due to rain without any rescheduling. Despite these issues, the restaurant staff were excellent, always kind and attentive. However, I noticed no real distinction in the premium beverages included with The Reserve.

Heavy rain also caused hallway flooding, nearly causing an accident. While I understand the circumstances, it highlighted a lack of preparedness. In the end, aside from Kelvin’s service, the upgrade added no real value the room design was identical, and the experience did not justify the price. I hope management reviews these gaps so The Reserve truly reflects the quality Meliá represents.

reviews.text: Our stay at Paradisus Palma Real was extremely disappointing and far below expectations for a family resort of this category. We had booked a full week but left after only three days due to a series of unacceptable situations. From the start, there was no staff available to help with our luggage. A large group had arrived before us, and we were left to carry our own bags despite traveling with two small children (ages 2 and 5). Housekeeping was another serious problem. We checked in on Friday, and by Saturday at 3:30 p.m. our room still had not been cleaned. I requested service since my 2-year-old uses diapers and the trash already had a strong odor. No one came until 10:00 p.m., after I had to take the trash outside myself and complain in the lobby. This neglect is unacceptable. On Saturday morning, while having breakfast, we were horrified to find a cockroach walking on our table. This was unsanitary and unacceptable in any resort, especially one claiming to be luxury. The most upsetting incident occurred Sunday night. While quietly watching TV with my children, security knocked on our door to complain that our baby had been crying and that we were being noisy. I was shocked and outraged. At a family resort, it is natural for a 2-year-old to cry. For security to treat us this way was humiliating. What was meant to be a relaxing family vacation turned into stress and frustration. I had no choice but to request a refund and urge management to address these failures.

reviews.text:
We recently stayed at your property and unfortunately, our overall experience did not meet our expectations. The main reason we chose the hotel was because of the photos and descriptions online, which made it appear as a high-quality destination. However, the real experience was far from what was advertised.

Room & Service
The room itself and basic amenities were average, but the service was inconsistent and unprofessional. Room service was not attentive and came across as too casual. Additionally, the language barrier created repeated communication problems, making even simple requests unnecessarily difficult.

Food & Dining
One of the most disappointing aspects of our stay was the food. Although the property promotes multiple dining options and cuisines, the quality was very underwhelming. Aside from breakfast, the meals did not feel fresh—many items seemed reheated or prepared long in advance, with desserts especially tasting like they were several days old. The "all inclusive" concept also felt misleading, as there seemed to be conditions or limitations attached to a number of items and services. Overall, dining here did not match the promise or expectations of a quality resort experience.

Front Desk & Management
Our biggest dissatisfaction was with the front desk and supervisory staff. Service at the front desk was slow, disorganized, and at times dismissive. The impression we got was that having a “manager” or “supervisor” was more for show.

reviews.text:
We recently stayed at this resort and had a mixed experience. On the positive side, the staff was consistently friendly, welcoming, and very responsive—definitely the highlight of our trip. The resort is walkable, which made getting around easy, and the pools and beach are conveniently accessible.

However, the overall experience fell short in a few important areas. The food was quite mediocre across the board. The buffet was inconsistent in both variety and quality, and most of the restaurants left a lot to be desired. The two standouts, Blue Agave and La Flora, offered much better dining—but unfortunately, La Flora was adults-only, so as a family with kids, we couldn’t enjoy it.

Although the resort is marketed as family-friendly, it seems more suited to older adults. Many areas were designated as “member exclusive,” yet they remained empty throughout our stay. The pools were deeper than expected and not ideal for younger children, and the beach was covered with sargassum and seaweed, which limited our time there.

Overall, we’d rate the experience a 3.5 out of 5, primarily because of the excellent staff. With a few improvements—especially around food quality and family accommodations—it could be a much more enjoyable destination for all types of travelers.

reviews.text:
We returned to Paradisus Palma Real in April 2025 after a great experience in 2023. Having stayed in many North American resorts, this review reflects a seasoned perspective.

1. The food remains excellent—diverse, high quality, and consistent with our last visit. I hope they maintain this standard.


2. The resort is exceptionally clean.


3. Staff are friendly and helpful across the board.


4. The beach is beautiful. We’re not sun-lovers, so the shaded huts near the water with comfy beds were perfect for relaxing while enjoying the sea breeze and view. It’s calmer than Aruba but still lively.


5. Restaurants are a highlight—the food, design, and ambiance are top-notch. The oceanfront breakfast buffet is especially memorable, both for the food and the stunning view.


6. Nightlife has improved since 2023, with better music and dancing. My wife loved it. Be sure to reserve restaurants in advance.


7. The pools are great—our child had a blast.


8. The kids’ club is excellent. Our child enjoyed it both times.


9. The spa is available, though we didn’t use it. That said, upselling spa services doesn’t work unless there’s a clear value. What makes it better or unique? We all get spa services in our countries. Why should we get it here with higher or same price?
They also have photography service which i found to be very overpriced.

Overall, this resort continues to impress and deliver a great family experience.

reviews.text:
The resort is well-maintained and overall quite nice. Most of the staff is friendly and helpful, though a few were less so—which seems to be fairly common in Punta Cana based on past experiences.

The buffet offered a wide variety of options daily, which we appreciated—thankfully, it wasn’t the same food every day. However, it was noticeable that some leftover food was repurposed, so I’d recommend being selective with your choices. It would be ideal if all buffet staff wore hair nets, and if guests were required to sanitize their hands before entering.

Our room had been upgraded with new bedroom furniture, which was clean and comfortable. The bathroom, however, had not been updated. The shower didn’t drain properly, the tiles were worn, and we did notice some mold.

The beach was beautiful and well-kept, cleaned daily by the staff. The beach service was excellent, especially if you tip—Jefry stood out and provided amazing service! One downside was the persistent vendors approaching guests to sell items.

The à la carte restaurants were decent—our favorite by far was Agave. It was a nice change of pace from dining at the buffet every day.

Lastly, our concierge, Antonio, checked in with us daily and made sure we were enjoying our stay, which we really appreciated.

reviews.text:
Paradisus Palma Real Golf & Spa Resort has been one of my favorite all-inclusive resorts in the world, and this was my second time staying here. My first trip was during the pandemic, and despite the restrictions, I had an absolutely amazing experience. The resort is beautiful, the food is top-notch, and the service is generally fantastic.

However, I have to say that my most recent experience was marred by one major issue: the resort's strict policy on outside excursions. For over a decade, I’ve been using Viator and booking excursions all around the world without issue. I arrived in the Dominican Republic with a list of pre-booked activities, only to find out that the resort doesn’t allow any outside companies to pick up guests for excursions. This was incredibly frustrating, especially since I had already paid for the excursions in advance.

To make matters worse, when I asked about arranging a car service to the airport (since outside services aren't allowed), I was quoted an outrageous $300 for a simple transfer. Meanwhile, my group's airport transportation to the resort in a suburban was only $70. This felt like a blatant attempt to funnel guests into the resort's own overpriced excursions and transportation services, which seemed like a monopoly and left a very bad taste in my mouth.

It’s disappointing to see a resort with such a strong reputation engage in practices like this that feel exploitative. While the resort itself is still beautiful and offers a great all-in

reviews.text:
I recently spent five nights at an all-inclusive resort in Punta Cana, and unfortunately, I left feeling disappointed. Despite promises of luxury and convenience, several aspects of the stay fell short.

One of the biggest issues was securing reservations for specialty restaurants. Over my five-night stay, I couldn’t get a spot at any of them, which was frustrating for an all-inclusive experience. The buffet, while offering variety, often served food that was cold and of questionable quality. To make matters worse, service was incredibly slow, despite the staff being friendly and trying their best.

On the positive side, housekeeping was excellent—our room was consistently clean and well-maintained. However, the room service app was never functional, adding to the inconvenience. The beach area was well-kept, and the resort did a good job managing the sargassum, which was a nice touch.

The resort also wasn’t ideal for families with young children. The pool area was limited, and there were few kid-friendly activities or amenities. I was also told I could access the nearby Melia water park for free, but later learned there was a fee and I had to watch a long "video" (likely a timeshare pitch) to get passes.

Though the staff was friendly, slow service and poor communication made it hard to fully enjoy the stay. Given these issues, I wouldn’t return to this resort, especially when there are better options in the area, particularly for families.

We stayed over American Thanksgiving break in 2024 (2 adults, 3 kids aged 12, 10, and 5) and had a wonderful time. The property is gorgeous - lush, well-maintained landscaping; beautiful, spacious corridors, gorgeous trees, nice breezes to be had everywhere. Lots of wide, smooth paths of travel - important to us since one of our  children uses a wheelchair. We had connecting rooms with lots of space for our crew. The in-room amenities were great - toiletries, continually re-stocked minibar, wonderful bed and bedding. No complaints about the rooms!
The kids enjoyed the Kidsdom (daycare) immensely, the staff was wonderful and they had a lot of fun activities for the kids. 
The beach was beautiful, plenty of lounge chairs. There was even a boardwalk that allowed my daughter to access the beach in her wheelchair. There are a good number of vendors that come by to sell experiences and products, but a simple and polite but firm “no Gracias” sent them on their way. Speaking of experiences, we did the dolphin Island experience and thought it was well worth it. Lots of memories and great photos from that.
Back at the hotel, we really enjoyed the pool area. The pool is massive, so even at peak times it never felt crowded. We spent a lot of time with the staff at the swim up bar and they were friendly and attentive. The pool does get pretty deep, but there is a kiddie pool area near the main pool.
The buffet satisfied all of us, and we enjoyed the Japanese and steakhouse restaurants.

reviews.text: My family and I stayed at the Paradisus Palma Real Golf & Spa Resort in Punta Cana, but our experience was overshadowed by several frustrating issues, particularly with check-in, concierge service, and communication. We were told we could check in early, but our room was not ready upon arrival. Despite being assured it would be ready within an hour with a promised upgrade, we were given a smaller room than what I reserved. This led to a frustrating process of room changes. The second room only had one king bed, unsuitable for our family of four. The third room was spacious and met our needs, but it wasn’t immediately available. After waiting over two hours, I had to escalate to the manager before finally receiving the correct room at 5:00 PM—hours after we arrived, wasting much of our first day. Our assigned concierge, Jose, also caused multiple issues. He failed to secure dinner reservations twice, leaving us embarrassed at the restaurants. Later, Antonio replaced him, and the service improved. Unfortunately, when Jose was reassigned, the quality of service declined again. Daily minibar restocking, which was supposed to be standard, never occurred despite repeated requests. Our room also lacked an iron or ironing board upon arrival, and it took over a day and multiple complaints to receive one. On a positive note, the food was delicious, and the restaurant and beach staff were friendly and welcoming.

**The Cleanliness:** The resort was impeccably maintained. Everywhere we went, from the lobby to the pool area and especially our room, everything was spotless. It was clear that cleanliness is a top priority for the staff, which made us feel completely comfortable and relaxed throughout our stay.

**The Staff:** The service at Paradisus Palma Real was truly exceptional. Every member of the staff went above and beyond to make sure our stay was perfect. reviews.text:
The only reason I gave this resort 2 starts (instead of 1) is because I had the best massage of my life from Alba.

The resort itself was quite pretty, but that was about it.  If you have any physical limitations, this is not the resort for you.  Our room was on the 3rd floor of a walk-up building.  What if you had a stroller or were someone with a cane (the steps were VERY slick stone).  

  In regards to the food, for a "family friendly" resort, the food availability was not.  Breakfast didn't open until 7 AM and ran until 11 AM and no lunch until 12:30 PM!  This may work for kids who sleep late, but I don't know many of those!  When we expressed surprise, we were told we could order from room service.  There are only 5 items on that menu for lunch or dinner: quesadilla, pasta with cream sauce, pasta with red sauce, a cheeseburger and chicken fingers.  That's it!  All of the food was mediocre at best, even in the restaurants.  Also nobody tells you that there is wine by the glass available, they only place a wine bottle list on the table.  Talk about poor service.

Unless you are an MVP, no one ever checks on you by the pool.  No one offers you drinks or even water.  The bartender was curt, only wanted to chat with his friends, or do shots with other guests.

We decided to leave a day early and we were literally harassed for 40 minutes by staff.  There are MUCH better all-inclusive hotels out there. Go there instead!

El resort es hermoso, la habitaciones increíbles. La atención me quedó debiendo. Primero, a pesar de haber reservado ONLY ADULTS no nos pusieron la pulsera de The Reserve hasta que nos llevaron a la habitación y tuvieron que gestionar aparte el cambio de pulsera. Segundo, cua do llegábamos a la habitación el minibar no estaba lleno o las cosas de baño como tissues o papel no estaban repuestas, días tuvimos que llamar para que nos hagan el refill del mini bar múltiples veces. En la piscina de “The Reserve” el staff era un poco rudo, recuerdo que un día preguntamos por toallas y en vez de pasárnoslas nos respondió “allá están” y se fue. Un día pedimos room service y cuando terminamos e íbamos a salir llamamos para que vayan a ver los platos a lo que nos dijeron que “los dejemos afuera en el pasillo que ya los pasaban a ver” sin embargo, como 6 horas después que llegamos, seguían los platos sucios fuera de la habitación con insectos. En el restaurante de carne tuvimos que esperar más d una hora para que nos pasen la comida y el término de la carne no estaba como lo pedimos y por último, al momento de salir llamamos para que nos ayuden a bajar las maletas en una hora determinada y a pesar de que se comprometieron NUNCA llegaron, tuvimos que bajar por nuestra cuenta. 
No todo fue malo, el restaurante dominicano estuvo excelente, Yaleidi como concierge fue muy atenta y la mejor atención en servicio fue para Norlejandro en el restaurante Sante, lástima que lo conocimos el último dia

reviews.text:
We were a party of 17 spread across 7 rooms. While the property location and aesthetic is great, the challenges are:
1) They do not have hotel shuttle from the airport so you have to haggle for taxi fairs as soon as you get off after a long journey.
2) Please expect a sub par experience if you have not booked directly with them. Thats also a great marketing strategy to get you in thousands of dollars worth of membership. Might suggest you to finance that.
3) While the restaurants have great 5 star aesthetics, food is not of the greatest quality. It is much worse if you are big group size as they will not give you the option of a la carte for "maximum efficiency". Even though this entire group had to individually pay for their room and not under one group discounted deal.
4) they did try to make up for their ineffeciencies after repeated complaining by bringing the menu of one of their Italian theme restaurant but serving in the general buffet place which is outdoor and now my kids who are allergic to mosquitoes are left with huge swellings on their body. 
5) Finally, please expect a very sub par drink quality with very limited option. For example, if you are a beer drinker, you wont even get a corona and similar for any alcohol of choice. Again a great marketing strategy to get you in for the expensive membership.
While I look forward to visit Punta Cana again, I am not keen to re book to this property or any other hotels under the Melia group. Discl# These are my personal op

reviews.text:
The view and property were beautiful and they about where the good part of this review ends. 

The restaurant reservation system was poor. The staff was not friendly and not helpful in providing advice. The Buffett offerings were ok not 4 star resort quality. 

Once you did get a reservation at one of the restaurants, you had to wait even though most of the tables were empty. Then once in the reserved restaurant you waited even longer for food. While at least 10 waiters and cooks stood around. It was something out of the ordinary. I’ve never experienced this level of inconsistency from a resort. From arrival at a reservation to leaving took at least 2 hours. Most of that time consists of waiting. 

Buffet was also a hassle because you had to track down a waiter to get drinks, coffee, water etc. Most tables were not cleaned in a timely fashion and sat with food on them for birds to feed on. 

Next: trying to sell you in the circle “timeshare.” Our concierge Lisette’s sole purpose was to try to get us to take this circle club timeshare meeting. Not to assist with reservations, excursions, hotel amenities offered. Do not get sucked into this garbage. The resort has exclusive sections where you can’t sit and swim. So that’s the circle club membership. It was completely off putting. 

The final complaint I have is regarding rooms service picking up the plates of food from the room after asking and requesting in the app. No one shows up so we had dishes piled on the counter.

reviews.text: The property itself is beautiful. The pools the beach its all beautiful. The food and service how ever not that great. Food was actually not good, besides breakfast. The restaurants on the resort took forever to seat you and serve you. The second night there we had reservations at the steak house for 9pm. We were seated till 10pm and food wasnt served till 10:45pm and my wife is 7 months pregnant. Most of the staff took there sweet time to do anything. We called the front desk 3 times and went to the front desk another 2 times asking for a bottle opener. Each time they told us some one will bring it to your room in a few minutes. They never came. I tried reaching the our concierge through expedia and emails, they never responded back. We had to leave the resort property 3 times to get a proper diner. reviews.text:
I will be short: The Hotel was beautiful!!! The Food was very bad in the first 3 days of our stay because the hotel was hosting a large construction convention from Canada and we saw no to bad service and food!
By the time the convention was over and everyone left , we started seeing very good food in the self service restaurant.  The steak restaurant was a JOKE unless you paid for the $95 Tomahawk.  My husband paid $50 for ribeye (I know it was supposed to be all inclusive) and his ribeye was thin and elastic and half of steak was fat.  I ordered a NY steak (that’s how they call it on menu) and I sent it back twice.   One because they brought it out rare (I asked for med-well) and the other reason was that I could really play tennis with it as a racket.  The steak was so stiff! 
The muscles in the Italian restaurant were old (I am from Boston) I think I can recognize fresh muscles.  
The SERVICE was so hit or miss! The first 3 days we got none but after that it ALL depended WHO you got! Some were plainly rude , argumentative and or just dismissive! Some got gave you lip service as if they are helping you.  There were some that genuinely were service oriented and those were the ones I Tipped! Yes I tip.  Most people come to these resorts and don’t.  I see it all the time.  We did end up getting re invited to the steak house for a free tomahawk because after sending back my steaks twice , I also asked for the manager.This place needs upper mgmt change or better training.

This property is a mixed bag. Aesthetically, it is beautiful. Lots of areas to relax in, pools are clean, and some staff were very kind. The downside is a bad one - trying to find a restaurant to eat on property is akin to participating in the Hunger Games. 

We have 3 rooms, 7 people and every day we have been told that it is not possible for us to eat dinner together at any point of our 4 day trip. This is absolutely ridiculous. Upon arrival, only one of our party members were told that there is a whatsapp chat with the property in which we can make dinner reservations. We have attempted to reach out daily and without any proper response. Guests are expected to stand in a line by 9am to book dinner reservations. On our first day, we went to reception and guest services twice to do this and they told us they could do nothing to help us. Then, they told another member and myself that they WILL put us down for dinner reservations for day 2 and 3. Day 2 morning and we stood in the reservation like just to find out we have been lied to and there was no reservation made. They have split up 7 people in 3 different restaurants at three different times. 

They lied to us about the whatsapp, about the reservations, and on their website. They do not care to help you. They did not help us make a reservation at a restaurant off property. The two dinners we have had made us wait 2  hrs.

Ensuring we have food should not be a concern for a trip we have paid around $1k per person for.

reviews.text:
Overall we enjoyed our stay at the Paradisus Palma Real resort. The proximity to the beach as well as the cleanliness of the place is commendable. There are some things that we felt were not upto out expectations. 
But let me start with the pros
1. Right next to the beach. You can just walk across from the hotel room to the beach.
2. Quiet- the adults section is seperate from the family section so things are quiet and peaceful. You hardly hear anything but the waves when you step outside the room 
3. Convenient location: not very far from the airport (35 mins drive) and right next to Punta Cana downtown..

Cons:
1. The food was bad. In every restaurant and buffet place inside the resort. I read bad reviews about the food situation here and wasn't expecting much, but those bad reviews are still an understatement to how horrible the food was. The first night we got in late and ordered food via room service. We ordered at 9:30 and the food came around 11:45. And it was a pain calling room service and asking for an update. 
The Japanese restaurant is a joke with the teppanyaki show more for entertainment than food. And the entertainment was not very entertaining. The other restaurants weren't any better. We found the rice always undercooked, meat overcooked, sea food raw and bland. 
2. We were not contacted by the concierge till the last day of the trip. To compensate for this, after we complained, they gave us extended late check-out. (Which we appreciate though)

reviews.text: The facility was overall beautiful and the staff were very kind but there is room for improvement's. When I arrived I was not greeted with a glass of wine as the package that was selected upon purchase. I had to wait in line to check in which I was then brought into another room to check in which I should have started there. The room was beautiful I must say but there was a dead bug on the floor which wasn’t cleaned prior. I gave it two or three days to see if the cleaning service would notice it but they didn’t. In fact I had to call them to clean my room. Depending on the color of your arm bracelet your suppose to get a concierge which I met mine not upon arrival but two days later. I was also informed that others got wine sent to the and their treats on the table were stocked when they came back to their room each day. I never got that and I asked for a bottle of wine. reviews.text: The property and rooms seemed new and was clean. Modern and spacious. plenty of bars. pool and beach clean and never a problem finding a chair or spot. Needs improvement on service staff especially concierge/reception. Definitely seemed understaffed. Everything was handled through Whatsapp chat which means there was no physical person waiting at any spa, reception, dining reservationist, even concierge. At check in, we somehow got forgotten amongst our friends therefore was never provided a full tour, any info on the property, or a concierge until I walked up to complain a day later. their resort app needs updated- some restaurants that say were open were closed. restaurants are small and gets booked up quickly due to lack of tables and staff. food is not readily available at all times except for room service (no poolside or beachside grill or afternoon snack). Definitely dont like the "upselling" at an all-inclusive. everything should be included- not have a menu with price options for better alcohol or better food everywhere we went. we even paid extra money for the "reserve" when booking which was advertised as having "top shelf liquor and extra lounge". after trying to find where this place was, it was an empty room with liquor on a table with no staff and nothing different than the other bars. Having been to many other all-inclusives I would say this property really missed the mark- I would not recommend staying here compared to other bigger names in the area.

reviews.text: If you’re used to the level of customer service and attention to detail of Cancun, Mexico, do not even consider visiting this resort. It’s evident that most workers simply don’t care about your needs and will try to avoid any initial requests you may have by saying it’s impossible. The food at any restaurant is quite sub-par and the food is terribly under seasoned. No matter where you go in the resort there is an issue with the food. It’s always either terribly chewy, undercooked, or charred to a crisp. Food options are extremely limited, especially for kids who are often forced to consume nothing but terribly bland chicken nuggets that have been sitting under a heat lamp for hours. There are also security concerns with peddlers on the beach constantly harassing guests to buy parasailing tickets or go snorkeling. These people are not only very persistent and don’t let you rest, they also try to extort unknowing guests for money and in some cases steal belongings when nobody is around. Hotel staff and management lured me into a timeshare presentation with the promises of a “special lunch” as well as “room and service” upgrades. Upon listening to these people try to lock me into a contract for several decades and politely declining, they provided no services that were initially promised by just listening to their presentation. Essentially, I was robbed of several hours of my time. The grills at the buffet are questionably dirty just like everything else in the buffet.

reviews.text: Save yourself the time and money and book elsewhere. Although the property itself is relatively nice, the staff and service made this the worst vacation we have ever been on. First, we were put in the wrong room and then told we had to wait 2-3 hours for housekeeping to clean our correct room. We went to a pool bar and within minutes, one of the guests said "I hope your stay is better than ours." We went back to the front desk and were told they were waiting on a call from housekeeping that our room was ready.  While waiting, another guest was attempting to get change and warned us that food and service were terrible. We made it to our room and the A/C was not working. We were told to call the front desk and they would send maintenance. Maintenance never showed up. This is an all-inclusive resort, yet we were told we couldn't have certain brands of liquor. "Reservations" have to be made each morning by your concierge for dinner or you are not "allowed" in the restaurants to eat. Multiple times we ate in the same buffet restaurant because no reservation was made for us. The front desk was not able to help with reservations or make change. The icing on the cake was when we asked an employee for change and he walked off with our money. The "Guest Relations" manger offered to make us a reservation at a restaurant. Laughable. We literally had to explain that this was theft and no, a reservation was not an acceptable solution. No apology was offered.

The rest of the trip I ate packaged food from the gift shop. Finally the second to the last night before leaving we  ate cheese pizza from the Italian restaurant.

I read the reviews and all were amazing and even a 5 star resort.  We booked it right Unfortunately, the resort was not what we had expected.  There are three resorts within the gated property which are all “sister resorts”. Paradisus Palma Real within itself is a very beautiful resort with an open concept all throughout the resort. There is no AC throughout the resort. Only in the rooms, stores, and restaurants. Which is no big deal but Punta Cana heat is a very dry heat and it does get very hot so you will be sweating when you are outside. 
The ladies in the front desk area were very nice and welcoming! 
One huge issue which we encountered that we were not aware of when I booked the resort is the dining situation. For breakfast and lunch there is only the buffet option. For dinner there is the option of buffet or at one of the restaurants. In order for you to dine at one of the restaurants you must have a reservation. And for the reservations you have to go the day of to a booth that is located near the buffet area. You can only do Reservations from 9am-4pm. Literally you have to be there by 9 am in order the get a decent reservation time or even to get a reservation at all. If traveling with small children you can only do two restaurants or the buffet. The other are adults only. The food itself is really good just wish on daily basis there was different variety of food.
Some employees were very rude and expect a tip every time. The sauna is located at the sister resort

reviews.text:
The room was spacious and comfortable, providing a relaxing environment. The resort itself was not overcrowded, which made for a more tranquil atmosphere.

However, there were a number of drawbacks that affected my overall experience. The customer service, except for Rafael at one of the restaurants, fell short of expectations. While Rafael did his best to accommodate our requests, the general service was lacking.

The quality of food at the buffet and restaurants was below average, leaving much to be desired. Additionally, the drinks throughout the resort seemed watered down, which was disappointing. Another drawback was the lack of air conditioning in common areas, including the elevator and massage parlor. This made for uncomfortable experiences outside of the rooms.

The absence of late-night activities and limited night-life options left me wanting more in terms of entertainment. Furthermore, the restaurants and shows ended early, which restricted evening plans. The shows themselves were uninspiring and failed to captivate the audience.

To add to the frustrations, the host insisted I leave a positive review as I was leaving, which felt manipulative and inappropriate considering the circumstances.

We reserved 2 Nikte swimups rooms which are supposed to include extra benefits ("Destination inclusive" is the name they use), concierge, etc. Well, we never meet the concierge (not even a call, I assumed he didn't believe it was important to call his assigned guests); and the staff was not aware of what was included in this type of room. We checkedin AFTER 3:30pm, then were moved to another room after 5:30,  but then we realized we were assigned to a room where the pool was almost empty. We were asked not to use the pool of the swimup (you buy a swimup to use the pool next to it, right?? so it makes no sense); they fixed the issue with the pool the next day. Both room's minibars were empty; we told them that, but when we got to our room after dinner, at 12am the minibars were still empty (not even drinking water); we were thirsty and called service room to get at least water; but the never showed up...
I have been 4 times at this hotel including this last time; and the reason we went now was to see the final renovation. These swimup rooms are part of this renovation; so I don't understand how many bad things are related to these rooms if they are new...
